Like public libraries and food banks, we exist to serve everyone, not profit from your attention.
That's why we don't run ads or put knowledge behind a paywall.
Wikipedia's here to satisfy your curiosity and give you the facts you need.
Wikipedia is free to use, but not free to provide.
An unprecedented rise in hardware costs is making the essential equipment needed to keep Wikipedia available to everyone much more expensive.
Your donation helps our nonprofit meet those costs while keeping Wikipedia free and independent.
"There is no place for violence in our Republic,” French President Emmanuel Macron said in a message on X.
Those who vandalized property, attacked government offices and businesses, and even looted our town halls will be prosecuted and punished.
“We will stand united against those who sow chaos … and who prevent people from peacefully expressing their demands,” Macron added.
In Paris, police fired tear gas and water cannons to push back people wearing hoods and masks and throwing fireworks, paving stones and other objects at officers in the Place de la République, northeast of the Paris city center.
Associated Press reporters saw thick black smoke rising from cars, bicycles and other vehicles, and trash bins on fire.
A newspaper kiosk also burned, while several shops were looted.
Several people have been injured in the clashes.
Many metro stations were closed Saturday at police request, including those around the Champs-Elysées and near the presidential palace, parliament and government offices.
Meanwhile, the majority of peaceful protesters joined a march that moved toward northwestern Paris.
